content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Secondary safety endpoint lacks a stated analysis",
      "quote": "AEs, serious adverse events (SAEs), and AEs leading to discontinuation or death, and severity of AEs as assessed by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0)",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint is listed but no specific statistical analysis method is described for it in the statistical methods section; only general safety assessments are mentioned.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the safety analysis (e.g., incidence, severity, relationship) in Section 9.6."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary efficacy endpoints lack analysis details",
      "quote": "Duration of response, defined as the time from date of first documented response (CR or PR) to date of documented PD, based on RECIST v1.1 by BICR",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "DOR, treatment response in non-injected target lesions, and OS are listed as secondary endpoints but no analysis methods are described for them in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Specify analysis methods for DOR, non-injected lesion response, and OS (e.g., Kaplan-Meier, summary statistics)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of the study is the ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1 as determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR).",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition lacks a full estimand: no explicit intercurrent event strategy (e.g., how to handle death, progression, or missing data) and no summary measure beyond proportion.",
      "fix": "Define the estimand for ORR including intercurrent event handling (e.g., treatment policy, composite) and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for PK endpoint",
      "quote": "Blood concentrations of CMP-001 or its metabolites",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PK endpoint is listed but no PK analysis methods are described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Add a PK analysis subsection describing parameters, models, and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for immunogenicity endpoint",
      "quote": "Development of anti-Qb antibodies",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The immunogenicity endpoint is listed but no analysis method is described.",
      "fix": "Add a description of immunogenicity analysis (e.g., incidence, titers, impact on safety/efficacy)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for exploratory biomarker endpoints",
      "quote": "Baseline, and change from Baseline, in tumor or blood measurements of biomarkers related to TLR9, immune checkpoints, and potential markers of resistance or response to immunotherapy",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "2.2.3 Exploratory Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Exploratory biomarker endpoints are listed but no analysis methods are described in the statistical methods section.",
      "fix": "Add exploratory analysis methods for biomarker endpoints, including handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inconsistency: 69 vs 100 subjects",
      "quote": "A sample size of 69 subjects achieves at least 90% power to detect a difference of 13% using a 2-sided exact test with a significance level of 0.05, assuming that the null hypothesis for ORR is 7% (Hodi-2016; Ribas-2018), and the study ORR is 20%. The sample size was increased to 100 subjects to adjust for an early discontinuation rate of 15% and to allow for a robust assessment of safety.",
      "page": 80,
      "section": "9.1 Sample Size Calculation",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size calculation is based on 69 subjects, but the study enrolls 100. The text explains the increase but does not clarify whether the power calculation is still valid for 100 or if the 15% discontinuation is accounted for in the primary analysis.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the power calculation is based on the evaluable population and that the 100 subjects account for discontinuations, or provide a revised power calculation for 100."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "Categorical variables will be summarized as the number and percentage of subjects within each category (with a category for missing data, if applicable).",
      "page": 80,
      "section": "9 Statistical Methods",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The general summary mentions a missing data category, but no specific imputation or sensitivity analysis for the primary ORR endpoint is described.",
      "fix": "Specify how missing response data will be handled in the primary analysis (e.g., non-responder imputation) and any sensitivity analyses."
    }
  ]
}
